cells.action:
RED FIRST: write the failing tests before the code and watch each fail for its own reason. Drive the external tool through fakes only: a fake CLI script named by BEE_DESIGN_OS_CLI that prints a canned `ui gate --json` object, and a fake node named by BEE_DESIGN_NODE_BIN that prints a version.

(1) VERB (per D5). Add verbs/design_group.rs with `bee design gate [--write] [--json]`, wired like tmp sweep: `if let Some(code) = tmp_group::try_native(args, t0) {` in verbs/mod.rs gains a design_group sibling; router.rs gains `"design gate [--write] [--json]",` beside `"tmp sweep",`; add a `design.gate` entry to src/generated/registry_payload.json in the same shape as `tmp.sweep` (name, invoke, surface, description, parameters, examples, deprecated) and keep tests/registry_contracts.rs and the cli-shape guard (hooks/cli_shape.rs) green. Port the field ratchet /mnt/data/Projects/anphabe/anphabe-goglbe/scripts/design-gate.mjs: pages = host config design.pages (a list of globs, read with crate::state::read_config_raw), default every *.html under the repo root skipping hidden dirs, node_modules, target, dist; per page run `npx --yes ease-design@0.6.1 gate <page> --dir . --json` with cwd = repo root, or `<node> <BEE_DESIGN_OS_CLI> gate <page> --dir . --json` when that env var is set (the BEE_GH_BIN pattern in verbs/report.rs); a non-zero exit with JSON on stdout is still a result (the field script does the same). Read data.errorCount, data.warningCount and data.tokenCoverage.overall.coverage (absent coverage = 0). Baseline file .bee/design/gate-baseline.json {version, pages: {<page>: {errors, warnings, coverage}}}, coverage rounded to 4 places. Rules: a page with no baseline entry must have 0 errors; errors may not rise; coverage may not fall. Clean -> one summary line, exit 0. Any regression -> one line per page naming it and the numbers, exit 1. Malformed tool output -> exit 1 naming the page and that the output was not the expected JSON.

(2) WRITE IS A HUMAN ACT. `--write` records the baseline for every page and refuses, writing nothing, while any cell in this repo's store has status claimed (a record with status "claimed", as handlers_select.rs reads it), naming the claimed cell ids.

(3) NO NODE (owner answer 1). Before any page, check `node --version` (or BEE_DESIGN_NODE_BIN). Missing, unparsable, or major below 20 -> print exactly `design gate: not run — Node 20 or newer is missing`, write .bee/design/last-run.json {"status": "not-run", "reason": "node-missing"}, exit 0. Every run that does run writes .bee/design/last-run.json {"status": "ran", "pages": <n>, "regressions": <n>}. This file shape and the exact line are a contract dob-6 reads; do not change them.

(4) SKILL TEXT. In packages/bee/design/bee-design/SKILL.md replace the raw npx call in the Check step (`npx --yes ease-design@0.6.1 gate <page.html> --dir . --json` at :77, and the `ui <command>` note at :41 where it concerns the gate) with `bee design gate`, saying the not-run line is what a Node-less machine prints and that the proof reason must then carry `design gate not run`. Make the same change in packages/bee/agents/bee-design.md.tmpl and in DESIGN_CELL_PREAMBLE (prompt.rs `pub(crate) const DESIGN_CELL_PREAMBLE: &str = "Design cell:`). Then rewrite the rendered agents with `bee dev regen` using the freshly built binary, and the release manifest with `bee dev release-manifest --write`. Revert any regen change outside this cell's files (.gitattributes, .bee/onboarding.json).

Tests: clean pages -> exit 0, one line; error rise -> exit 1 naming the page; coverage fall -> exit 1; new page with errors -> exit 1; new page with 0 errors -> exit 0; malformed output -> exit 1; --write with no claimed cell writes the baseline; --write with a claimed cell refuses and writes nothing; node 18 -> exact not-run line, exit 0, last-run.json not-run; a ran run writes last-run.json ran; design.pages globs limit the pages.

cells.action:

(1) WHEN THE RULE BINDS (owner answer 2). Read the host config with `pub fn read_config_raw(root: &Path) -> Map<String, Value> {` (state.rs:161). The rule binds only when design.packs is an array with at least one entry. design.packs absent, "none", or an empty array -> the cap behaves exactly as today.

(2) UI CELL (per D6). A cell is a UI cell when any path in its `files` matches design.ui_globs (config list of globs; default *.html, *.css, *.scss, *.jsx, *.tsx, *.vue, *.svelte, matched against the file name at any depth). Put the binding test and the glob match in a small new module verbs/cells/design_rule.rs (declared in verbs/cells/mod.rs) so the cap and the add warning share it.

(3) CAP REFUSALS, in handlers_close.rs with the cheap pre-checks beside `if js_trim(&proof_command) != cell_verify {` (:308), before any write, each naming its fix in the house refusal shape (`capCell: cell "<id>" refused — <what>. FIX: <remedy>`): (a) a UI cell whose verify does not contain `bee design gate` -> refuse, FIX: add `bee design gate` to the cell's verify (bee cells update while open) and run it; (b) a UI cell where .bee/design/last-run.json has status "not-run" and the proof reason segment does not contain `design gate not run` -> refuse, FIX: say in the proof reason that the design gate did not run because Node 20 or newer is missing; when it does contain it, the cap is accepted (owner answer 1); (c) any cell, UI or not, whose `files` include .bee/design/gate-baseline.json -> refuse, FIX: the baseline is recorded by a person with `bee design gate --write` when no cell is claimed. last-run.json shape (contract with dob-5): {"status": "not-run", "reason": "node-missing"} or {"status": "ran", "pages": n, "regressions": n}; a missing or unreadable file means no not-run requirement.

(4) EARLY WARNING. In bee cells add (handlers_write.rs), when the rule binds and a UI cell's verify lacks `bee design gate`, print one stderr warning naming the cell and the fix; never refuse, never change the cell.

Tests: no-pick host, UI cell without the gate -> cap accepted (unchanged); picked host, UI cell without the gate -> refused with the FIX text; picked host, UI cell with the gate in verify -> accepted; picked host, non-UI cell -> accepted; last-run not-run and reason lacking `design gate not run` -> refused; same with the phrase -> accepted; a cell listing .bee/design/gate-baseline.json -> refused in a picked and a no-pick host; design.packs "none" -> unchanged; cells add warns on stderr and still adds the cell.

in a host with no pick the cap behaves exactly as before
in a picked host a UI cell whose verify lacks bee design gate is refused with the fix named
a not-run record requires the proof reason to say design gate not run, and then the cap is accepted
a cell listing the baseline file is refused
cells add warns on stderr and still adds the cell
